# retrieval-eval-v1 — Stage-1 ground-truth evaluation design (proposed, CP-4.3D planning)

Date: 2026-09-28. Status: **Accepted and FROZEN** (D-021, approved by the user 2026-09-28) before
any Stage-1 retrieval result exists. Changes after this point require a new, dated amendment section
that states whether any result had been seen.
Statistics: `scripts/ladrag_stage1_design_stats.py` →
`experiments/ladrag/results/design/retrieval-eval-v1-stage1-stats.json` (read-only; no model, no API).

## 0. Question and evaluation principle

**Question:** do the cross-page relations generated by LAD-RAG† ingestion improve retrieval of the
official MMLongBench-Doc gold evidence pages, especially for multi-page questions?

- Ground truth is **page-level** (`question → evidence_pages`). There is no official node-to-node edge
  ground truth, so graph quality is evaluated **downstream**, by page-level retrieval (PR, IPR).
- The CP-4.3C relation audit (19 edges) is an **AI-assisted qualitative diagnostic audit**: failure
  analysis evidence only — not ground truth, not edge precision/accuracy, not a benchmark metric.
- Every rule below that the paper does not specify is **[RECONSTRUCTED]**. None of A–D is the full
  LAD-RAG agent; they are controlled diagnostics of the graph's contribution.
- All rules are fixed here, **before** any retrieval result on these questions exists.

## 1. Subset retrieval-eval-v1 (Stage 1)

Definition: all pilot-v1 questions of the five documents already used in CP-4.3C (CAL-0001). The
documents were chosen for calibration before any graph retrieval existed, so they are not selected on
retrieval results. pilot-v1 is not modified. Question IDs are listed in the stats JSON.

| Document | Type | Pages | CAL-0001 pages | Not yet ingested | Q | Evidence | No-evid. | Multi-page |

| 2305.14160v4.pdf | Academic paper | 16 | 1–8 | 8 | 6 | 5 | 1 | 2 |
| f8d3a162…pdf | Administration/Industry file | 17 | 1–6 | 11 | 10 | 9 | 1 | 5 |
| reportq32015-…_95.pdf | Research report (image-only) | 34 | 7–10 | 30 | 10 | 8 | 2 | 5 |
| mi_phone.pdf | Guidebook | 37 | 4–7 | 33 | 9 | 7 | 2 | 3 |

## 2. Full-document ingestion requirement and reuse of CAL-0001

Each Stage-1 document is ingested **completely** (all 132 pages), so retrieval also sees distractor
pages. The partial CAL-0001 graphs are **not** used for evaluation.

Reuse of cached model replies (content-addressed cache, R16), assuming CAL-0001 settings are kept
(1280 px, 8192 tokens, same prompts and model):
- 2305 p1–8 and f8d3 p1–6 (14 pages): the calibration started at page 1, so a full-document run
  reproduces the same working memory → all calls are expected to be cache hits (verified from the
  run's `cached` counts, not assumed in results).
- reportq3 p7–10, mi_phone p4–7, Campaign p5–9 (13 pages): calibration started mid-document, so the
  working memory differs → only node extraction (step A, image + fixed prompt) is reusable;
  section queue / graph construction must be re-run.
- 105 pages are new.

Changing resolution (1600 px) or the token limit would invalidate the cache for all 132 pages.

## 3. Compared retrieval conditions [RECONSTRUCTED]

Common to all: per-document retrieval (the question's own document only); neural node index as in
R10 (E5-large-v2 pinned, text = `summary + "\n" + content`, 512-token windows / 64 overlap, node score
= max window score, E5 `query:`/`passage:` prefixes); ties broken by node ID. Seeds = the top
`m = 10` nodes (`semantic_search.top_k`, R10). Nodes are mapped to their physical page.

| ID | Condition | Graph used |
|---|---|---|
| **A** | Semantic-only: rank all nodes; pages in order of first appearance | none |
| **B** | Semantic + one-hop expansion of the `m` seeds over **all** generated edges | intra-page + cross-page |
| **C** | Same procedure as B with cross-page edges removed (ablation) | intra-page only |
| **D** | Control: same procedure as B, neighbours = physical pages p ± 1 of each seed page | none (layout only) |

Notes fixed in advance:
- **C vs A:** intra-page edges only reach nodes on the same page, so at page level C must equal A.
  C is kept as a sanity check of the expansion code; the effect of generated cross-page edges is
  **B vs C**.
- **D** is the structure-free control: 13 of 18 multi-page questions have only adjacent gold pages,
  so "add the neighbouring page" is a strong trivial alternative. The graph is useful only if B
  beats D, not only A/C.
- Community expansion (`get_community_for_node`, Louvain over a graph that includes cross-page edges)
  is a possible secondary variant (B-comm vs C-comm with communities recomputed without cross-page
  edges); it belongs to CP-4.4 and is not part of the primary Stage-1 comparison.
- Edge direction is ignored (graph is undirected, R7); rejected relations are never used.

## 4. Fairness: budget-controlled comparison [RECONSTRUCTED]

Graph expansion must not "win" by returning more pages. Two views, both fixed now:

**(a) Matched distinct-page budget, frozen k ∈ {1, 3, 5, 10}** (primary). Deterministic page
ranking; no rule uses gold evidence:
- A: distinct pages in order of first appearance in the full node ranking.
- B / C / D (interleaved rule): walk the seeds in semantic rank order; for each seed emit its own page,
  then its neighbour pages, skipping pages already emitted. After the `m` seeds, continue with A's
  remaining pages in A's order. Stop at k distinct pages.
  - B / C neighbour order: the seed's one-hop neighbour nodes (B: all edges; C: intra-page edges only)
    sorted by (1) neighbour physical page number ascending, (2) neighbour node ID (canonical
    `page_N-obj_KKK` order); each contributes its page.
  - D neighbour order: p − 1, then p + 1 of the seed page p (ascending page number, consistent with
    B), omitting pages outside 1..num_pages.
  - Tie-breaking of the semantic ranking itself: score descending, then node ID.
- Hence at every k all conditions return exactly min(k, pages in document) pages; expansion
  **displaces** lower-ranked semantic pages rather than adding pages. PR@k and IPR@k are compared.

**(b) Unbudgeted set view.** A-set = pages of the `m` seeds; B-set = A-set ∪ pages of one-hop
cross-page neighbours; D-set = A-set ∪ {p ± 1}. Report PR, IPR **and |P̂|** (mean pages returned)
side by side; a PR gain with a larger IPR/|P̂| is reported as a trade-off, not as an improvement.

## 5. Metrics and reporting

Primary metrics: Perfect Recall (PR) and Irrelevant Pages Ratio (IPR) (CP-1.2/1.3 definitions), on
evidence questions. **Primary subgroup: multi-page evidence questions (18).** Secondary: all evidence
(35), single-page (17), Figure (12), Chart (10), Table (3), Pure-text (18), Layout/generalized text
(8). Source groups **overlap** (a question with several sources is in each of them) and are not
mutually exclusive. No-evidence questions (8) are reported separately (NoEvidenceCorrect / IPR,
D-008/D-009); every condition returns pages, so they are expected to be uninformative here.

Statistical interpretation (frozen): Stage 1 is **exploratory / diagnostic** — five documents only.
- Per-document results are **required** for every condition and k.
- The paired question-level bootstrap of D-017 (`scripts/compare_retrieval_runs.py`; B vs C, B vs D,
  B vs A; mean PR/IPR difference, 95 % interval, 10,000 resamples, seed 0, win/tie/loss) is reported
  **descriptively**.
- A whole-document (cluster) bootstrap [RECONSTRUCTED] is a **sensitivity analysis** only.
- **No confirmatory or significance claims.** Groups with < 10 questions (Table, Layout, per-source
  multi-page cells, per-document cells) receive descriptive results only.
- Page-text baselines (EXP-0001–0003 rankings, already computed for pilot-v1) are shown on the same
  35 questions as external reference only.

Resource failures (R22): a gold page on a page with `status = resource_failure` is reported as an
**ingestion resource failure**, separately from retrieval misses and from pages ingested successfully
without nodes; such questions are also reported with and without exclusion. Graph files list these
pages in `metadata.provenance.resource_failed_pages`.

## 6. Graph-reachability diagnostic (deterministic)

For each evidence question, with S = pages of the `m` seeds, N = pages of one-hop **cross-page**
neighbours of the seeds not in S, G = gold pages:

| Outcome | Rule |
|---|---|
| semantic already complete | G ⊆ S |
| expansion completes | G ⊄ S and G ⊆ S ∪ N |
| expansion adds some missing gold (not all) | (G \ S) ∩ N ≠ ∅ and G ⊄ S ∪ N |
| expansion adds only irrelevant pages | N ≠ ∅ and N ∩ G = ∅ |
| no expansion possible | N = ∅ |
| gold unreachable | G \ (S ∪ N) ≠ ∅ |

Additionally: number of irrelevant pages added (|N \ G|); for each missing gold page the shortest
graph distance from the seed nodes (1, 2, 3+, unreachable) and whether it is also p ± 1 of a seed page
(i.e. whether the graph found anything the layout control would not); gold pages with **zero nodes**
(ingestion failure) counted separately, because they are unreachable by construction. Reported for
m = 10 (primary) and m = 5.

## 7. Stage-1 ingestion estimate (not a result)

Estimated no-cache model time per page from CAL-0001, per document (2305 392 s, f8d3 538 s, reportq3
80 s, mi_phone 92 s, Campaign 278 s), applied to the pages still needed; node extraction is ≈ 35 % of
model time and is reused for the 13 mid-document cached pages:

| Document | New pages | Re-run B–D only | Estimate |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2305 | 8 | 0 | ≈ 0.9 h |
| f8d3 | 11 | 0 | ≈ 1.6 h |
| reportq3 | 30 | 4 | ≈ 0.7 h |
| mi_phone | 33 | 4 | ≈ 0.9 h |
| Campaign | 23 | 5 | ≈ 2.0 h |
| **Total** | **105** | **13** | **≈ 6 h (plausible range 6–9 h)** |

Upward risks: the working memory keeps growing over 28–37-page documents (graph construction cost
grows with it; CAL-0001 only saw ≤ 8 pages per document), runaway calls (≈ 8 % × 5–6 min), and the
2305 appendix pages. One overnight run with resume.

## 8. Is Stage 1 informative?

- 35 evidence / 18 multi-page questions in 5 documents. With paired binary PR, a difference is
  distinguishable from zero only if it is large (roughly ≥ 4–5 net wins among 18 multi-page
  questions); document clustering widens uncertainty further.
- Stage 1 is therefore adequate as a **go/no-go diagnostic** (does the graph reach missing gold pages
  at all, and more often than p ± 1?), and to validate the evaluation code end to end — **not** for
  confirmatory claims.
- Stage 2 would add the other five pilot-v1 documents (109 pages, 37 questions, 10 multi-page;
  pilot-v1 total 80 / 28 multi-page). Even pilot-v1 is small; a larger, rule-selected document set
  may be needed later (to be decided after Stage 1).

## 9. Dependencies CP-4.3D → CP-4.4 → CP-4.5 → evaluation

| Step | Needs | Provides |
|---|---|---|
| CP-4.3D Stage 1 (GPU, ≈ 6–9 h) | approved settings (resolution, runaway, OOM) | full-document graphs of the 5 documents |
| CP-4.4 symbolic retrieval (CPU) | graph file format (exists) | neighbour lookup with edge filters (intra / cross-page), graph queries, communities — used by B, C and §6 |
| CP-4.5 neural node index (GPU, minutes) | graphs from CP-4.3D for real runs (CAL-0001 only for tests) | node ranking → seeds for A–D |
| Evaluation (proposed new CP, e.g. CP-4.5A) | 4.3D + 4.4 + 4.5 | A/B/C/D, reachability, D-017 comparisons |
| CP-4.3D Stage 2 | Stage-1 go/no-go outcome and user approval | remaining pilot-v1 documents |

CP-4.4 and CP-4.5 can be implemented and unit-tested without Stage-1 graphs, but no evaluation
number is produced from partial (CAL-0001) graphs.
